title: Impact on Singapore of Construction of Kuala Linggi International Port in Malacca
what_it_is: Impact on Singapore of Construction of Kuala Linggi International Port in Malacca

sections.label: KLIP oil storage capacity impact
sections.summary: KLIP's planned 1.5 million cubic metre oil storage capacity is not big relative to Singapore's 20.5 million cubic metres, and expansion completion is a decade away.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The expansion is expected to be completed only within the next decade, so it is still too early to determine the exact impact on Singapore's economy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Our preliminary assessment, however, is that KLIP's planned oil storage capacity of 1.5 million cubic metres is not big, relative to Singapore's current capacity of 20.5 million cubic metres.

sections.label: Minimal container transhipment impact
sections.summary: The expansion should have minimal impact on Singapore's container transhipment port.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The expansion should, therefore, have minimal impact on Singapore's container transhipment port.

sections.label: Pasir Panjang automation and bunker metering
sections.summary: New berths at Pasir Panjang Terminal Phases 3 and 4 have a fully-automated yard crane system, and Singapore is first to require mass flow metering for bunkers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: For example, the new berths at Pasir Panjang Terminal Phases 3 and 4 feature a fully-automated yard crane system, which raises port productivity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Singapore is also the first port in the world to require bunkers to be delivered via a mass flow metering system.

sections.label: Tuas terminal capacity and monitoring
sections.summary: The Tuas terminal, with capacity up to 65 million TEUs, is expected to be the world's largest container terminal, and Singapore will monitor KLIP and regional developments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: With an annual capacity of up to 65 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs), the Tuas terminal is expected to be the largest container terminal in the world, allowing us to achieve greater economies of scale and more efficiently handle the mega ships of the future.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The port will also incorporate new automation and technologies to further boost efficiency and productivity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: We will closely monitor KLIP and other regional developments and their potential impact on Singapore and take further measures as necessary to retain our competitive edge.

sections.label: Investments to attract shipping companies
sections.summary: Activities and significant investments aim to ensure commercial considerations tilt shipping companies' calculations in favour of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, the first thing we must do is to ensure that the product that we offer to them, the services that we offer to them, meet their requirements and, in fact, allow them to make a better go of their commercial considerations than if they were to call at other ports.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, all of the activities and the significant investments that we are making are geared towards ensuring that, commercially, the considerations will tilt the calculations of the shipping companies in favour of Singapore.
